ApiError.description: The body of every non-2xx response.

AttestProfileRow.description: One profile, as the attestation projections hold it. `credential` is the governance credential this profile CLAIMS, in its CIP-129 rendering -- a claim, not a proof: nothing on chain checks that the claimant controls it, and more than one profile may claim the same one. `credential_is_script` is that identifier's header byte decoded, so a consumer never has to parse bech32 to tell a key credential from a script one. `slot` is the only time a projection row carries, published raw because this service holds no slot configuration.

AttestationDetailResponse.description: One attestation with its disputes inline, read in a single transaction so they are the same snapshot. At most 50 disputes travel; GET /disputes?target=<id> is the paged view.

AttestationRow.description: One attestation. `date` is the issuance time and IS bounded by the minting transaction's validity interval; `claimed_period` is SELF-REPORTED and never chain-verified, with both bounds present or neither. Rendering the two alike claims something the chain never said. `accepted` is the subject's acknowledgement.

items.description: This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.
This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.

date.description: This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.

CommitteeMemberStatus.description: A committee member's standing, derived from committee_de_registration alone. Two values, not Koios's four: expiry is published beside it as expiration_epoch, because a member whose term ends in a future epoch is serving today.

DisputeRow.description: One dispute against an attestation. `verdict` is null while the dispute is OPEN. An upheld dispute is published beside the attestation it contests and never hides or deletes it. `deposit` comes back to the opener either way -- there is no punitive verdict, so losing one costs network fees and nothing else.

opened_at.description: This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.

EpochParamsSummary.description: The protocol parameters a client needs to audit a published tally. Threshold lists are (name, value) pairs under db-sync's own column names, so any of them can be looked up in palmares.thresholds. `gov_action_lifetime` is the parameter, not the voting window: the ledger sets expiration = proposed_epoch + lifetime + 1.

EpochParticipationPoint.description: One epoch of DRep participation. `dreps_voted` counts voters and `votes_cast` counts votes; they differ by re-votes. The rate is null only when no DRep held power that epoch -- zero is a real reading and preprod epoch 311 has it.

ErrorCode.description: Every reason this API refuses or fails a request, as a stable snake_case tag. Branch on this, never on the message: the message is for people and may be reworded, the code is the contract. The status each one is served with is fixed -- the 400 group is a bad request, the 404 group a well-formed request naming nothing, 429 a rate limit, the 503 group an index that is not ready yet, and internal_error a bug here.

GYAssetClass.description: This is an asset class, i.e. either "lovelace" or some other token with its minting policy and token name delimited by dot (.).

MetricFormula.description: One published formula. `sql` is the statement the server actually executes, inlined from the same embed the query path reads, so the documented formula cannot drift from the served number. Exactly one of `sql_file` and `sql_object` is set, so every formula_id resolves to something a reader can go and look at. `params` names the positional placeholders in bind order.

PowerBucket.description: One bucket of the voting-power histogram, half-open [lo, hi) in lovelace, with `hi` null on the open top bucket. Inclusive edges would double-count a DRep sitting exactly on one, and the counts would stop summing to the page total.

SPOSummary.description: One stake pool in the current voting-power distribution. `ticker` and `participation_rate` are null throughout F1 -- the first because db-sync's pool-metadata fetcher is disabled, the second because no spo_participation_rate_v1 exists in the metric catalog yet.

SearchResults.description: Six groups, always present. `total` is across the whole match; each group's `items` is is capped at `limit_per_group`. A hit with no published text carries its identifier as its `title`.

StatusResponse.description: Service identity, chain freshness and protocol parameters in one request.

SyncStatus.description: How far behind the chain this index is. `lag_seconds` is measured from the tip block's time; `is_ready` is /ready's own verdict.

TreasuryWithdrawalRecord.description: One treasury payment a governance action would make. `enacted_epoch` is the only authoritative enactment value db-sync has; `enacted_at` is epoch-only, with slot and tx_hash always null. `paid_heuristic` is a guess from (stake_address, spendable_epoch) and is ambiguous when one address receives two withdrawals in one epoch.

info.description: Read-only queries over the Cardano governance record: DReps, governance actions, votes, delegations, the constitutional committee and treasury withdrawals. Every row comes from a view over cardano-db-sync — there is no projection table and no second derivation — and every published metric carries the id of the formula that produced it, resolvable at /metrics/formulas.
info.title: Palmares Query API

get.description:
Every governance event on one timeline, newest first: DRep registrations, updates and retirements; votes; proposals; vote-delegation changes; committee hot-key authorisations and resignations; and the ledger's own epoch-boundary outcomes (ratified, enacted, expired, dropped, and a treasury withdrawal paying out). 
Paged by CURSOR, never by offset: an offset over a feed that grows at the head re-shows rows the previous page already showed. Two directions, and at most one of them per request: `before` walks backwards in time for an infinite scroll, `since` walks forwards for a catch-up poll and returns its page in ASCENDING order. Neither means newest-first from the tip. Both at once is a 400 `both_cursors_given`, because the two would name different directions for one page. 
Pass back the `next_cursor` the previous page carried. A page shorter than `limit` is the end of the feed in that direction and carries no `next_cursor`. `total` is always null -- counting 3.9M union rows on every page is the cost this endpoint exists to avoid, and a count from a different pass than the rows is a count that disagrees with them. 
`offset` is not a parameter here. Servant ignores an undeclared query parameter, so `?offset=10` is served as the unpaged request it is rather than refused. 
The five epoch-boundary kinds have `at.slot` and `at.tx_hash` null TOGETHER: they happen in the ledger at an epoch boundary with no transaction to point at. `at.epoch` and `at.time` are always present. 
`actor_id` and `target_id` are text whose meaning depends on `event_type` -- a credential in hex, a stake address in bech32, or a governance action id. `actor` matches either form, so `drep1y...` and its 56 hex characters find the same events.

get.description:
Every attestation one profile has issued about another. One endpoint rather than a route per direction: `subject` is a track record, `issuer` is an issuance history, and both together is one actor's statements about another. 
`date` is the ISSUANCE time and IS bounded by the minting transaction's validity interval. `claimed_period` is SELF-REPORTED and never chain-verified, which is why it is not a filter and not a sort key -- a range query over it would read as though the chain had checked it. Both of its bounds travel or neither. 
`accepted` is the subject's acknowledgement. It filters both ways and has no default, so the unfiltered list is the whole record including claims nobody has accepted. 
`date_from`/`date_to` bound `date`, inclusive; a reversed range is 400 `invalid_time_range` rather than an empty page. Default ordering is date descending.

get.description:
One attestation with its disputes INLINE. Inline and not a second request for the reason /gov-action/{id} inlines its tallies: a client that fetches the challenges separately will render the attestation before they arrive, and an undisputed-looking attestation is exactly the wrong thing to show for a disputed one. 
An upheld dispute is published BESIDE the attestation and never hides or deletes it, so `disputes` being non-empty is the whole signal -- read `verdict` on each, which is null while that dispute is open. 
At most 50 disputes are inlined; a dispute costs a deposit, so more than that against one attestation is a funded adversary rather than a shape to expect, and an inline list has no offset to escape with. `GET /disputes?target=<id>` is the paged view. 
The attestation and its disputes are read in ONE transaction, so they are the same snapshot. 404 `attestation_not_found` when the id names nothing.

get.description:
The committee the ledger is currently applying, with its quorum, the governance action that established it, and its seats inline. `epoch` is the epoch of the epoch_state row that names this committee, so a client can see which moment the answer is as of. 
Each seat is identified by its COLD credential, the identity that survives a hot-key rotation, with the signing hot key published beside it -- the same choice /votes makes. preprod shows why at scale: 648,767 hot-key registrations resolve to 43 cold credentials, and `votes_cast` counts distinct governance actions through all of a member's registrations so one record does not split across rotations. 
`status` has two values, active and resigned, not Koios's four: it is derived from committee_de_registration alone, and expiry is published beside it as `expiration_epoch` rather than folded in, because a member whose term ends in a future epoch is serving today.

get.description:
One row per stake address: the delegation it currently holds, and whether that delegation still counts. Not one row per certificate -- a superseded certificate is not the latest one, so it is not a row here, and `is_current=false` means one thing only: the stake account was deregistered AFTER the delegation's certificate. preprod has 2,304 addresses that have ever delegated, 2,015 of which currently count. 
`is_current` DEFAULTS TO TRUE and filters both ways, which is a deliberate difference from /drep/{id}/delegators, where is_current=false widens to the history instead. 
`drep_id` accepts a credential in any form -- drep1y..., drep1..., 56 hex characters -- and also either reserved ledger option. Those two are not a special case: of the 2,015 current delegations, 1,020 name drep_always_abstain and 40 drep_always_no_confidence, so the reserved options hold the majority of delegated stake. 
`lovelace` is the stake the ledger counted at the latest snapshot and is null for an address with no stake in it.

get.description:
Every headline figure in one request and one transaction: how many DReps there are and in what state, how much stake is parked on the two reserved ledger options against how much is delegated to real DReps, every governance action by type and by state, what is still votable, what closes next, the treasury's requested and enacted totals, the current power leaderboard, and DRep participation epoch by epoch. 
The DRep counts, the leaderboard rows and the closing-soon rows are /dreps' and /gov-actions' own -- the same queries, so no figure here can disagree with the list it links to. `total_dreps` is the universe /dreps lists by default (registered = active + inactive); `retired_dreps` is published beside it, never inside it, because preprod has 511 retired against 294 registered. 
`power_epoch` is its own field because the ledger writes the DRep stake distribution one epoch behind the tip, so the three lovelace figures are a different moment from everything else and say so. 
`actions_in_flight` is `last_votable_epoch >= epoch`, which is not `state = proposed`: measured 12 against 11, the extra one being an action whose state already reads expired while its window is still open. 
The treasury is TWO numbers because 83 withdrawals are recorded on preprod and none has been enacted, so one field called `withdrawn` would be either 0 -- true, and reads as no treasury activity -- or the requested total, which is a lie about the word.

get.description:
Every profile the registry has projected from chain: who it says it is, what kind of actor it stands for, and the governance credential it CLAIMS. 
`credential` is a claim and not a proof -- nothing on chain checks that the claimant controls the credential, and the same credential may be claimed by more than one profile. `claimed=true` narrows to the profiles that claim one at all, which is the subset a verification screen has anything to check. 
`credential_is_script` travels beside the string and is DECODED from its CIP-129 header byte, never inferred: a key credential and a script credential can share a hash and are not the same actor. 
`slot` is the only time a projection row carries -- a wall clock stamped at ingest would be re-stamped by every rollback replay -- and it is published raw, because this service holds no slot configuration and a second slot-to-time conversion that can disagree with the chain's is worse than a slot number. 
`q` matches name and description, case-insensitively, with any % or _ the user typed matched literally. Default ordering is registered_at descending.

get.description:
The verify direction: given a DRep credential, which profiles claim it. 
**CIP-129 ONLY.** `drep1y...` (key) and `drep1yw...` (script) are accepted; the CIP-105 form `drep1...` and 56 bare hex characters are REFUSED with 400 `invalid_drep_id`, although every other route here accepts all three. The reason is that neither of those two carries a header byte and `drep` is the HRP for both credential kinds, so neither can say whether the credential is a key or a script -- and the projection stores the full CIP-129 string the datum claimed. Accepting one would mean choosing a header byte to compare against, and choosing the key byte (which the governance routes do, then resolve the row by its 28-byte hash and re-render from db-sync's own has_script) would silently report every script DRep as a key DRep and find no claim for the script profile that exists. There is no row to ask here, so the caller is asked instead. 
A non-canonical bech32 spelling of an accepted form still matches: the id is decoded and re-encoded before it reaches the query. 
PAGED, and `total` is the answer to "is this contested": 0 is an unclaimed credential, 1 is a single claim, more than 1 means several profiles claim the same credential and this API does not pick a winner. Ordered OLDEST CLAIM FIRST, by slot, so the first row is deterministically the first claimant rather than whichever row the database returned first.

get.description:
One request behind the command palette: DReps by published name, governance actions by title or abstract, stake pools by ticker or metadata name, and any of them by a pasted identifier. Six groups ALWAYS travel, each capped at `limit_per_group`, so a missing section is an empty one rather than an absent key; `profiles` and `attestations` are always empty here and are filled over the attestation schema later. `total` is across the whole match, not across the page. 
A pasted identifier is matched by EQUALITY after its bech32 checksum verifies -- drep1y…, drep1…, cc_cold1…, cc_hot1…, pool1…, 56 hex characters, gov_action1… or <tx_hash>#<index> with the # sent as %23. A PARTIAL identifier is not matched: `pool1` is a prefix of all 686 preprod pools, so prefix-matching a five-character paste would return the whole table. 
Text matching is substring and case-insensitive, and a % or _ the user typed is matched literally -- measured, q=_a returns nothing where an unescaped pattern would return 39 hits. 
What is searchable is set by what db-sync has fetched, and on preprod that is narrow: 64 of 805 DRep credentials carry a name, 7 of 131 actions carry a title, NO pool carries off-chain metadata, and a committee member has no name in db-sync at all -- so that group answers an identifier and nothing else. A hit with no text shows its identifier as its title. 
Unlike /dreps, no status filter is applied: a retired DRep is still something you look up by name.

get.description:
The pools in pool_stat at its latest epoch -- 510 on preprod at epoch 320 -- ordered by voting power descending. This is the DISTRIBUTION, not the set of pools that have voted: 45 pools have ever cast an SPO vote and only 39 of those are still in the distribution, six voters having since retired. min_votes_cast=1 therefore returns 39, and /votes?voter_role=spo is the endpoint that answers who voted. 
`votes_cast` counts DISTINCT governance actions, not vote rows: one preprod pool has 8 rows across 4 actions. 
`ticker` is null throughout F1 because db-sync's pool-metadata fetcher is disabled and off_chain_pool_data has 0 rows. `participation_rate` is null because there is no spo_participation_rate_v1 in the metric catalog, and every number this API publishes carries the id of the formula that produced it -- a rate with no resolvable formula would break that contract. 
There is no `q` parameter: an SPO row is a direct pool_stat/pool_hash read with no text column to match. Exact id lookup is what /search is for.

Every treasury payment a governance action would make, across all actions -- the list form of the `withdrawals` block inside /gov-action/{id}. preprod has 83 of them across 82 actions to 19 beneficiaries. 
NONE has ever been enacted, so `enacted_epoch` and `enacted_at` are null on every row and `paid_heuristic` is false on every row. `enacted_epoch` is the only authoritative enactment value db-sync has; `enacted_at` is an epoch-boundary chain point with no slot and no transaction hash, because the ledger pays a withdrawal at an epoch boundary and there is nothing to point at. 
`paid_heuristic` carries its warning in its name: reward_rest has no governance-action key, so matching a payment by (stake_address, spendable_epoch) is ambiguous when one address receives two withdrawals in one epoch.

get.description:
Every vote cast, across all three voter roles, with the rationale anchor's outcome and the voter's power at the epoch the action's window closed. One endpoint rather than four per-actor routes: the filters are repeatable, so a DRep's record, an action's votes, a committee member's votes and the global feed are all the same query. 
`voter_id` accepts any identifier form -- drep1y…, cc_cold1…, pool1… or 56 hex characters -- and committee votes are addressed by the COLD credential, the identity that survives a hot-key rotation, with the signing hot key published beside it. 
Re-votes are returned as rows, not hidden: `revote_count` says how many exist for that (voter, action) pair and `is_final` / `is_first` mark which one a verdict or a latency is measured from. preprod's worst pair has 21,626 rows, from the epoch-187 committee stress test. 
There is no `has_rationale` parameter: it is `anchor_status=valid`, which makes the caller say which of the five anchor outcomes they mean instead of collapsing an unreachable IPFS document into "no rationale".

400.description: Invalid query parameters; the body carries a machine-readable `code`

404.description: Well-formed request naming something that does not exist

503.description: Index not ready: too far behind, no ledger state, or the wrong network
